ArcelorMittal SA Reports Steady Steel Export Volumes Amid Stable Market Conditions

ArcelorMittal SA, Luxembourg’s flagship steel producer, released its latest trade figures on Tuesday, showing stable export volumes in the first quarter of 2024 as international demand for European steel products remained consistent. 

The company reported total steel exports of 2.3 million metric tonnes between January and March, in line with the 2.31 million tonnes recorded during the same period last year. Revenues from export sales reached €1.62 billion, representing a marginal increase of 1.1% year-on-year, which the company attributed to favourable exchange rates and modest improvements in product mix.

Speaking on the results, ArcelorMittal SA’s Chief Commercial Officer, Paul Dumont, noted, “We continue to see healthy demand from our key markets in Western and Central Europe, as well as steady shipments to North Africa and Southeast Asia. The figures reflect the resilience of our supply chain and our ability to adapt to evolving customer needs.” Dumont added that the company is “closely monitoring input costs, particularly for energy and raw materials,” but indicated that current conditions remain supportive for stable operations.

Industry analysts described the performance as indicative of broader market stability. “The steel sector in Luxembourg and across the eurozone has entered a phase of consolidation after the volatility of recent years,” said Marie Fontaine, a metals market economist at the European Industrial Metals Forum. “ArcelorMittal’s export numbers are in line with sector norms, and there are no immediate signs of disruption on the horizon.”

The Luxembourg Steel Workers Union commented on the figures, highlighting the importance of sustained export activity for local employment. “Steady trade volumes help ensure that our members’ jobs remain secure,” said union representative Georges Weber. “We welcome the company’s ongoing commitment to responsible production and export practices.”

According to data from the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy, steel exports accounted for 17% of the country’s total goods exports in the first quarter, underscoring the sector’s strategic significance. Looking ahead, ArcelorMittal SA stated it expects demand to remain stable through the second quarter, supported by ongoing infrastructure projects and consistent orders from automotive and construction customers.
